title: The Billionaire Who Drove a 1993 Volvo

beats.say: He was worth $50 billion yet flew economy and bought clothes at flea markets.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of a silhouette of a person sitting in a cramped airplane seat, dim cabin lighting, moody atmosphere.

beats.say: This was Ingvar Kamprad, the founder of IKEA. And his frugality wasn't about suffering.
beats.visual: A dark, sleek 1990s Volvo station wagon parked on a wet cobblestone street at dusk, cinematic shadows.

beats.say: It was a system. He drove a 1993 Volvo for two decades because he hated waste.
beats.visual: Close-up of weathered hands holding a well-worn leather wallet, warm side lighting, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: He stayed in cheap hotels and always booked economy seats to keep his costs low.
beats.visual: A minimalist hotel room with a single bed, stark shadows, muted Scandinavian color palette.

beats.say: Most people think wealth means upgrading everything. Kamprad proved the opposite.
beats.visual: A stack of simple plain white paper notebooks and a cheap black ballpoint pen on a bare wooden desk.

beats.say: He treated personal spending like a business budget. Every single dollar had a job.
beats.visual: A close-up shot of a person tearing a used piece of paper in half to reuse the blank side.

beats.say: When you stop trying to impress strangers, your money finally starts working for you.
beats.visual: A minimalist wooden kitchen table with a single ceramic mug and soft morning light streaming through a window.

beats.say: He didn't pinch pennies out of fear. He did it to fund what actually mattered.
beats.visual: A wide shot of a vast empty warehouse with polished concrete floors reflecting soft overhead lights.

beats.say: He built a global empire by keeping his own overhead near zero.
beats.visual: An abstract close-up of dark wooden furniture joints fitting together perfectly, dramatic lighting.

beats.say: That's why true wealth isn't about what you spend, it's about what you keep, and that's exactly how
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking down a quiet city sidewalk away from the camera at twilight.

caption: Frugality isn't about suffering. It's about protecting your freedom. #money #personalfinance #wealth #frugalliving #ikea
description: Ingvar Kamprad built IKEA into a global giant while living below his means. True wealth is built by keeping your overhead low.
first_comment: What's one luxury you refuse to spend money on?

facts.claim: Ingvar Kamprad drove a 1993 Volvo and flew economy
